_comment: Wave-5.5 furniture ratchet baseline. Regenerated by scripts/ratchet/check.sh's own recompute logic — see that script for the exact find/rg commands, and scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py for the fourth metric, which needs a scanner rather than a pattern. Do not hand-edit the counts without rerunning them; hand-edit only the metadata fields (computed_at_commit, computed_date, bump_reason) when intentionally moving the baseline.
computed_at_commit: hyg/error-split-b after the twelve domain moves; measured by check.sh on that tree. The other three counts are re-measured unchanged from hyg/ci-docs-diffs at 52aef9ec.
bump_reason: LOWERED giant_files 3 -> 2. Nothing is raised and no other count moves: allow_attrs 98, print_macros 91 and process_global_statics 45 are re-measured unchanged on this tree and their _attribution blocks still hold. error.rs left the list because ONE-2001 split `Error` into twelve per-domain enums under error/ - see the giant_files _attribution's error_rs_left_2026_09_11 entry. Lowering a ratchet is free; raising one is a stated decision in the PR.

giant_files.description: Non-test .rs files with >= 800 lines. Non-test = path has no 'tests/' directory component, filename is not 'tests.rs', does not end '_tests.rs' and does not start 'tests_'. vendor/ and target/ excluded.

_attribution.summary: 188 -> 2. 106 over-bar production modules split into directory modules across eleven move-only batches, plus three single-function files streamlined semantically under the bar (api/openapi/descriptions.rs, sync/window/forward.rs, pipeline/execution/channels.rs), plus error.rs, which left the list when ONE-2001 decomposed `Error` into twelve per-domain enums under crates/oneiron/src/error/.
_attribution.verification: Every split checked move-only by scripts/refactor/tools/split_check.py against its base revision: no item added, removed, duplicated or altered in body. Zero exceptions across all eleven batches. Root surface held at 702 names throughout and the codemap was regenerated at every batch boundary.
_attribution.nothing_is_deferred_any_more: Every file still over the bar is over it for a stated structural reason below, not for scheduling.

remaining_2_and_why.voice_cascade/tts_spikes.rs (856): Reasoned indivisible (reader G25): the only clean seam is the cfg(test) mod tests, which drives private Adapter and Phase directly, so extracting it forces pub(crate) churn for zero runtime gain.
remaining_2_and_why.claim/lifecycle.rs (800): Reasoned indivisible (reader G26): one cohesive impl Vault of 18 chain-walk and gating methods, 733 lines, 91% of the file, shared across the supersede, reserved-supersede, retract and demotion paths. Exactly on the bar.

_attribution.error_rs_left_2026_09_11: error.rs was the third file and is gone from the list. It was capped by one item, the 1436-line `pub enum Error`, and the attribution said clearing it meant decomposing `Error` into per-domain types - a semantic redesign, owner call. That call was made (ONE-2001, DESIGN-error-enum.md option B): the 21 cross-cutting variants stay flat on `Error`, the other 203 moved into twelve `#[error(transparent)]` domain enums, one file each under error/. error/mod.rs is 565 lines and the largest child, error/sync.rs, is 529. Variant names, `#[error(..)]` strings and `ErrorKind` are byte-identical; Debug gains one wrapper level for moved variants.
_attribution.correction_2026_09_09: The earlier claim that four of the remaining files were ordinary splittable modules was itself over-counted by one: pipeline/execution/channels.rs holds a single associated item, not several, so it was never cuttable per item. Single-function files are accepted; semantic streamlining is a separate pass.

allow_attrs.description: Occurrences of '#[allow(' under crates/*/src, excluding test files (same non-test definition as giant_files).

_attribution.summary: +11 against the 2026-08-26 baseline. The +19 that this lane inherited all arrived on main before it started; the lane added zero and has since retired 8.
_attribution.arithmetic: 87 baseline, 106 at main 7eed085f, 106 at 5d7de40c, 98 after the bare-suppression retirements below. 20 additions minus 1 removal = +19, then minus 8 real fixes = +11.
_attribution.cause: The 239 commits between ce47e61e and 7eed085f, via ordinary feature work: ONE-1608 VaultReadClient, ONE-1887 failure ladder, ONE-1403 majority-vote judge, the deep-retrieval host, the MemoryReasonCompose API, the GitWire repo-lock refactor and provenance txn threading.

Commit 1a7aca7d split distance.rs into a directory module and the test moved to distance/tests.rs, a filename this metric excludes. Nothing was fixed or deleted; the occurrence crossed the test-exclusion boundary. That is why the net is 19 and not 20.
_attribution.debt_13_justified: 13 of the 20 carry an inline reason or doc comment arguing the case (memory/caps.rs x4, llm/step/step_claim.rs x2, code_run/vault_read/contract.rs with an explicit reason=, repo_mutation/queue.rs, attempt_queue/cancel/verbs.rs, oneiron-bench/src/beam/judge.rs, oneiron-server/src/server.rs, api/memory_reason.rs, api/memory_reason/deep_admission.rs). Several say plainly there is no production caller yet - for those the honest lever is deleting the code, not the allow.
_attribution.bare_suppressions_retired_2026_09_09: The 7 sites the 2026-09-09 audit found carrying a bare suppression with no stated reason are GONE, fixed rather than waived: 8 attributes in total, because the claim-write site covered two sibling doors. gate/doors/claim_write.rs:50 and :88 -> both pre-check doors take a ClaimGateWrite pack from the caller (new ClaimGateWrite::plain). store/retrieval_telemetry/run_store.rs:79 and :443 -> the four context-pack finalize seams thread one RetrievalRunFinalize value. oneiron-bench/src/interface_bench/eval_run.rs:21 -> ExpectedRowIdentity. provenance/writes.rs:361 -> EdgeProvenanceWrite. origin/smart_http/serve.rs:265 -> ExchangeSetup separates the exchange's fixed setup from its live handles. failure_ladder/lineage.rs:207 (clippy::large_enum_variant) -> the Healer arm carried the same AttemptRecord twice and the duplicate is deleted; the residual size gap (arms of 664, 3456 and 2040 bytes) is closed by boxing each arm's payload, taking the enum from 3464 bytes to 32, with the trade-off stated on the type. No #[allow] or #[expect] was added anywhere; the root-surface pin held at 702.

print_macros.description: Combined occurrences of println!, eprintln!, and dbg! under crates/*/src, excluding test files (same non-test definition as giant_files). Counted with word-boundary-anchored patterns so 'eprintln!' lines are not double-counted by a bare 'println!' substring match.

_attribution.summary: +3 against the 2026-08-26 baseline. All three predate the hygiene lane; the lane added zero.
_attribution.arithmetic: 88 baseline, 91 at main 7eed085f, 91 at 5d7de40c. Every other file is unchanged.
_attribution.cause: One new oneiron-bench CLI subcommand, "beam community", absent at baseline: oneiron-bench/src/beam/runner.rs:29 (its line of print_help), oneiron-bench/src/beam/arms.rs:160 (the success-path report) and arms.rs:164 (the failure-path eprintln).
_attribution.assessment: Not debug residue. All three are structurally identical to the println!/eprintln! lines the pre-existing smoke and run arms of the same CLI already print. The metric counts CLI output in a benchmark binary the same as a stray probe in library code; that is a limitation of the metric, not a regression in the tree.

process_global_statics.description: `static` items (including `static mut`) under crates/*/src whose DECLARED TYPE contains one of Mutex, RwLock, Atomic, OnceLock, OnceCell, LazyLock, 'Lazy<', 'Cell<', RefCell. A static inside a `thread_local! { ... }` block is EXCLUDED (per-thread by definition). Test-gated (#[cfg(test)]) statics COUNT: under `cargo test --lib` sibling tests share one process, so a test-only global is exactly the seam that flakes. Non-test file = the same definition as giant_files (no 'tests/' path component, filename not tests.rs / *_tests.rs / tests_*.rs); vendor/ and target/ excluded. Recomputed by scripts/ratchet/process_globals.py; `--list` prints every hit as `path:line NAME: type`.

_attribution.summary: ADDED 2026-09-11 at 45. This is a new metric, not a raised ceiling: no existing count moved. The scanner sees 106 static items under crates/*/src in non-test files; 45 meet the type test outside a thread_local! block, 48 sit inside one (already per-thread, the shape this ratchet wants), and 13 declare a type that does not name a wrapper - 9 genuinely plain, and 4 that hide one behind an alias or a struct (see known_gap_4_statics).
_attribution.why_it_exists: Two flakes in one week came from process-global mutable state that tests read or arm. #922: the BM25 diagnostics counters are process-wide, so a sibling test in the same `cargo test --lib` binary moved them under a test that asserted on them. #923: the delete rendezvous slot is a single process-global Mutex, so two raced-delete tests clobbered each other's channel; the fix made that seam thread-local. The class is being migrated to per-vault ownership in a later lane. Until then this counter stops it regrowing.

split_45.test_gated_seams_7: Reachable only under cfg(test) and therefore shared by every sibling test in one binary - the flake class itself. deletion/rendezvous.rs:214 DELETE_RENDEZVOUS (#923, the one that already lost its thread_local siblings), batch/export/foreign_stage/export_foreign_stage.rs:25 STAGED_IMPORT_ADMISSION_COUNT and :28 STAGED_IMPORT_FIRST_STAGE_BARRIER, outbound_intent_ledger/store.rs:26 FORCE_SYNC_CALLS, sync/client/federated.rs:26 STOP_AFTER_STAGED_IMPORT, oneiron-server/src/oauth_relay.rs:125 TEST_TRANSPORTS, and identity_topology/shell_edge_reconcile.rs:435 FULL_RECONCILIATIONS inside a #[cfg(test)] mod test_hooks.
split_45.production_counters_and_id_generators_14: Atomics that move on ordinary operation, so any test asserting on one is order-dependent: attempt_queue/telemetry.rs:16-18 (3, one of them an array), bm25/diagnostics.rs:6 (the #922 array), gate/decision.rs:13, repo_mutation/worktree.rs:17, session_overlay/overlay/segment.rs:28, store/open_gates/open_version_keys.rs:441, oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs:96, and five request/session id counters in oneiron-server (api/facade.rs:396, commands/api.rs:422, error.rs:555, livequery/error.rs:24, server/lifecycle.rs:18).
split_45.resource_locks_and_write_once_registries: Process-wide mutual exclusion over a process-wide resource, plus set-once registries and caches: the LMDB/vault-root open locks and the open-path map (store/open_gates/open_version_keys.rs:186/188/190), the GitWire repo-lock map and process env, the two staged-import admission locks, the bench probe hook, and fourteen OnceLock/LazyLock manifests, matrices, recognizers, MCP surfaces and caches. These are the least urgent third: a write-once registry is not a race, but it is still process state a second vault in the same process inherits.

_attribution.known_gap_4_statics: The metric reads the DECLARED type, so an alias or a named struct hides a global from it. Four real process-globals are not in the 45: store/test_hooks.rs:30 BEFORE_LMDB_OPEN and :37 AFTER_LMDB_OPEN (declared LmdbOpenHookSlot = LazyLock<Mutex<Option<..>>>), batch/export/foreign_stage/export_foreign_stage.rs:73 STAGED_IMPORT_PRE_CONTENT_HOOK (declared ArmedPreContentHook = OnceLock<Mutex<..>>), and oneiron-remote/src/embedded.rs:86 REGISTRY (a Registry struct holding an AtomicU32 and a LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap>>). Stated rather than silently fixed: resolving aliases needs a real type resolver, and widening the definition now would move the number away from the definition above. Do not use an alias to get under the bar - that is the same stated decision as raising it.
_attribution.expected_direction: Down. The per-vault ownership migration lane lowers this; lowering is free, raising is a stated decision in the PR (AGENTS.md ratchet law).

_metric_definition_gap_found_2026_09_09: CLOSED 2026-09-09. The non-test exclusion matched 'tests.rs' and '*_tests.rs' but not 'tests_*.rs', a spelling the repo also uses (branch_store_oracle/tests_leak_sweep.rs, api/git_http/tests_auth.rs, oneiron-bench/beam/tests_*.rs and 15 more), so those 18 files counted as production. check.sh now excludes that spelling too, in both the ripgrep globs and the giant_files find pipeline. NO COUNT MOVED: those 18 files hold zero '#[allow(' and zero print macros and none reaches 800 lines. This closed a latent hole before it could report a test file as a production giant; it did not relax any number.
